4.1 Generation in Cambodia 
4.1.1  Generation by Type of License 
Two types of licensees generate electricit y in the Kingdom of Cambodia. Independent 
Power Producers having generation li cense generate and sell electricity to suppliers or industries in 
compliance with the Power Purchase Agreement with that supplier or industry; and Consolidated 
Licensees having generation license as one of its licenses generate electricity for supply to 
consumers through their distribution system.   
 
The information on operation of generation system by Generation Licensees, Electricite du 
Cambodge and Isolated systems operated by Consolidated Licensees is given in Annex 3, Annex 4 
and Annex 5 respectively. The summary information about installed capacity and energy sent out 
by the Independent Power Producers, EDC and Consolidated licensees is given in Annex 2(b).  
 
The energy generated and sent out by all licensees in Cambodia during 2014 is 3,058.36 
GWh, which is 72.79 % more than the energy sent  out during 2013. The quantum of energy sent-

using coal and 4 – Plants using wood and other biomass. The major power plants added during

Sovanna Phum Investment Co., Ltd, connected to the Phnom Penh System and Cambodia Energy 
Limited, and C.I.I.D.G.Erdos Hongjun Electric Po wer Co., Ltd connected to National Grid, use 
coal to generate electricity. All other power plants  of the licensees are di esel power plants using 
Heavy Fuel Oil (HFO) and/or Light Diesel Oil (LDO). The summery information on installed 
capacity and energy sent out by type of generation is given in Annex 2(c) . Due to addition of 
Stung Tatay and full operation of Lower Stung Ru ssei Chrum Hydro power plants in 2014, the 
energy generated by Hydropower Plants increase d to 1851.60 million kWh in 2014 compared to 
1,015.54 million kWh in 2013. Similarly due to fu ll operation of coal plant of Cambodian Energy 
Limited and operation of one unit of coal plant of C.I.I.D.G.Erdos Hongjun Electric Power Co., 
Ltd in 2014, the energy generated by coal power plants increased to 863. 02 million kWh in 2014 
compared to 168.75 million kWh in 2013.

4.3.2  High Voltage Lines under implementation  
Following Transmission Line Projects are under construction and their position at the end 
of 2014 is stated below: 
i. 230 kV transmissionline from Kampong Cham to Kratie with substations at 
Kampong Cham and Kratie. The transmission line project is being implemented by 
L.Y.P Group Co., Ltd and is likely to be commissioned in 2017. 
ii. 230 kV transmission line from Kratie to Steung Treng with substation at Steung 
Treng. The transmission line project is being implemented by EDC and is likely to 
be commissioned in 2017. 
iii. 230 kV transmission line from Steung  Hav substation to Phnom Penh. The 
transmission line project is being implemented by Alex Corporation Co., Ltd and is 
likely to be commissioned in 2017.
